summary: The note describes a major overhaul of the city's architectural heritage protection laws introduced after September 1, 2023. The reforms broaden the definition of heritage, speed up designation, strengthen incentives and penalties, and extend protection to interiors. They are backed by new bodies and programs: the AHAC, Adaptive Reuse Policy, Heritage Conservation Fund, HRTF and the 'Heritage in the Neighborhood' initiative.
one_line: A city overhauled its architectural heritage laws between late 2023 and early 2024, adding new committees, funding, adaptive reuse rules, tougher penalties and community education.
key_facts: On October 15, 2023, the city council, led by Councilor Jane Doe, introduced comprehensive amendments to the architectural heritage protection laws.

The reformed policy broadens the definition of 'heritage' to include smaller, culturally significant buildings, streamlines designation of heritage sites, and enhances incentives for owners to maintain and restore properties.
Mayor Alice Wright called the enhanced incentives a "game-changer for architectural conservation."
The Architectural Heritage Advisory Committee (AHAC) was announced on September 22, 2023, by the Department of Urban Development.
The AHAC comprises architects, historians, urban planners and community representatives and oversees heritage designations and reviews renovation or demolition proposals.
The NGO 'Timekeepers', whose president is Emily Carter, welcomed the creation of the AHAC.
The Adaptive Reuse Policy took effect on November 10, 2023, encouraging owners to repurpose heritage properties for modern uses while retaining internal integrity where feasible.
Architect Laura Gibson called Adaptive Reuse "a win-win" that retains the city's soul and reduces environmental impact.
Revised regulations enacted on December 1, 2023, introduced escalated fines and restoration orders requiring violators to revert unauthorized changes at their own expense.
The reform extends protection to interior features of designated heritage properties, which Sandra Lee, who runs a local heritage tour company, praised.
The Heritage Conservation Fund (HCF), announced on January 20, 2024, provides grants and low-interest loans from a mix of public and private investment.
The Heritage Restoration Task Force (HRTF) works with the AHAC to provide technical assistance and monitor restoration quality; member Mohammad Al-Sayed is a civil engineer.
The 'Heritage in the Neighborhood' initiative, launched on February 9, 2024, offers workshops, walking tours and school education programs.
Historian Dr. John Goodwell was among the experts who advocated for the reforms.
